issue_paraphrase: When a SQLite table is defined with the two table options that disable rowid storage and enable strict mode at the same time, the generated CREATE TABLE statement joins the two extension clauses without a comma separator. Executing the generated DDL then fails with a syntax error at the second clause instead of creating the table.
fix_summary: SQLiteDDLCompiler.post_create_table was rewritten to collect the WITH-ROWID and STRICT extension clauses into a list and join them with ', \n', so multiple extension clauses are emitted comma-separated ('WITHOUT ROWID, STRICT') instead of being blindly concatenated with newlines.
notes: No external DB or network needed; sqlite bundled with Python 3.12 supports STRICT (>= 3.37). Single golden test runs in ~0.06s. The fix commit message references the issue as 'Fixes: #12368' / PR #12369.

issue_paraphrase: Reflecting table constraints from a SQLite database returns corrupted definitions for CHECK constraints whenever a CHECK constraint is followed by another kind of constraint, such as a UNIQUE or PRIMARY KEY clause, within the same CREATE TABLE statement. The reflected check-constraint text ends up with a trailing comma and the beginning of the following constraint appended to it, so the stored condition is no longer the pure check expression.
fix_summary: One-line regex fix in SQLiteDialect.get_check_constraints: the clause-boundary pattern was extended so that after a comma the lookahead also accepts UNIQUE, FOREIGN and PRIMARY keywords (not only CONSTRAINT/CHECK), preventing over-consumption of the following constraint clause. This repaired a regression introduced by the earlier fix for #11677.
notes: No external DB needed (sqlite:// in-memory). Full ConstraintReflectionTest class runs in <1s at 1 CPU. Fix commit: 'Fixes: #11832, Closes: #11834' (PR by a contributor). The pre-existing test_check_constraint is the one that fails at parent, so an author must run that test (the two new tests added by the fix pass on both ends).

FIX bd0da426: golden tests 2/2 PASSED; direct repro shows call 2: raw[T.a]=20 raw[T.b]=999. Buggy code confirmed present at parent by inspection (bulk_persistence.py has no adapt_to_context-disable / no ORM-load-exec-options merge for the RETURNING execution path).
install_recipe: pip install -e '.[asyncio]' 'pytest>=7,<10' pytest-xdist   # verified with greenlet 3.5.5, pytest 9.1.1, pytest-xdist 3.8.0
issue_paraphrase: When an ORM-enabled UPDATE statement that uses RETURNING is executed with the option that re-fetches changed objects from the database after the statement, the first execution returns correct values but on the next execution of an equivalent statement the returned columns are mislabeled: looking up a column object returns the value of a different column, so for example the value of the last RETURNING column is returned where the first was requested. The corruption occurs when the order of the columns in the .returning() clause differs from the order of the columns as declared on the mapped table, and it appears on any execution served from the ORM's compiled statement cache.
fix_summary: In _BulkUDCompileState._or_create_orm_setting (ORM bulk UPDATE/DELETE compile state), the ORM's load execution options (which include a flag disabling result-level adapt_to_context) are now merged into the effective execution options that are part of the cached construct. On a cache hit the ORM UPDATE/DELETE RETURNING statement is a 'two level' statement whose cached core level returns columns in mapper order while the ORM level carries the user's .returning() order; skipping the positional core adaptation keeps the cursor keymap consistent (Column-object index == string-name index) across cache hits.
notes: No external DB needed (sqlite supports UPDATE..RETURNING). Both golden tests run in ~0.05s. Only the [update] variant discriminates; an author should target CacheAdaptReturningOrderTest::test_returning_keymap_stable_across_cache_hit[update]. The direct repro checks result.raw (the underlying core result) because ORM-level row access re-processes positions and can mask the corruption. Requires sqlite >= 3.35 (Python 3.12 bundles 3.4x).

issue_paraphrase: Calling the session lookup method for a primary key on an object that is already present in the session's identity map issues a real SELECT against the database when the locking flag is passed as False rather than being omitted or passed as None. The same call without the flag, or with the flag explicitly None, short-circuits to the identity map and performs no query at all, so the False value defeats the intended no-database fast path.
fix_summary: Session.get() eligibility check for the identity-map fast path changed from 'with_for_update is None' to 'with_for_update in (None, False)', matching ForUpdateArg._from_argument which already treats False and None identically; passing False now also bypasses the database when the object is already loaded.
notes: No external DB needed (sqlite://). Whole parametrized golden test runs in ~0.13s. Only the [false] variant discriminates at the parent; the others pass on both ends, so a task oracle should run test_get_with_for_update_use[false]. The direct repro uses a before_cursor_execute counter.
